item.title: Freehold landowners' rights remain protected under Constitution – Vosarogo
item.description: Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources Filimoni Vosarogo has reassured freehold landowners across Fiji, that their property rights remain protected under the Constitution and the law, following statements attributed to SODELPA members proposing that all land in Fiji be placed under iTaukei ownership. Vosarogo says freehold landowners concerned about the proposal should be assured that their exis
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Lands and Mineral Resources Filimoni Vosarogo has reassured freehold landowners across Fiji, that their property rights remain protected under the Constitution and the law, following statements attributed to SODELPA members proposing that all land in Fiji be placed under iTaukei ownership.

Vosarogo says freehold landowners concerned about the proposal should be assured that their existing land titles and property rights remain protected.

He stresses that any acquisition of land by the State, must follow proper legal procedures and include fair compensation.

The Minister says there is no hidden agenda or threat to existing land titles, and is urging landowners not to be alarmed by statements that create uncertainty about land ownership.

Vosarogo has also expressed serious concern about SODELPA's statements on land ownership, describing them as irresponsible and potentially damaging to public confidence.

He criticises what he describes as confusion within the party, saying its representatives and leadership have given conflicting accounts of who authorised the statements.

Vosarogo says such statements are creating unnecessary fear among landowners at a time when Fiji should be focusing on economic growth, development and attracting investment.

He warns that uncertainty over property rights could undermine investor confidence, discourage investment and affect the livelihoods of Fijians.

The Minister also highlights that iTaukei people already own approximately 91 percent of the land in Fiji, and stresses that the Coalition Government will not undermine their land rights.

He says proposals that create uncertainty over existing land ownership arrangements risk dividing communities rather than bringing Fijians together.

Vosarogo stresses that the Government remains committed to protecting the property rights of all Fijians, regardless of ethnicity or background.

He is calling on political leaders to act responsibly when discussing sensitive issues such as land ownership and to place the interests of the country ahead of political differences.

Vosarogo says Fiji needs stability, investor confidence and unity rather than fear and uncertainty over land ownership.

item.title: Tavua Town Council workers go on strike over pay and allowance demands
item.description: Tavua Town Council workers are on strike today after the Council refused to sign a Memorandum of Agreement for their 2026 Log of Claims, which includes a cost-of-living adjustment and an increase in operational allowances. A representative of the National Union of Workers Fiji says the workers negotiated in good faith and reached an agreement with the Council last Thursday, but the Council went ba
item.content:encoded:
Tavua Town Council workers are on strike today after the Council refused to sign a Memorandum of Agreement for their 2026 Log of Claims, which includes a cost-of-living adjustment and an increase in operational allowances.

A representative of the National Union of Workers Fiji says the workers negotiated in good faith and reached an agreement with the Council last Thursday, but the Council went back on the agreement yesterday.

She says the Council has indicated that it is not in a position to meet the agreement.

The union representative says the Council was supposed to send a letter explaining its position, but the union has yet to receive it.

A meeting is currently underway at the Tavua Town Council to discuss the matter.

item.title: Passing of Assistant Minister Vocea a great loss to Fiji – Rabuka
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the sudden passing of Assistant Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management Jovesa Vocea is a great loss to his family, the Government and the communities he served. Rabuka has extended his deepest condolences to Vocea's family on behalf of the Coalition Government and the people of Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the sudden passing of Assistant Minister for Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management Jovesa Vocea is a great loss to his family, the Government and the communities he served.

Rabuka has extended his deepest condolences to Vocea's family on behalf of the Coalition Government and the people of Fiji.

He says Vocea's passing is a significant loss to his colleagues and the Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Risk Management, where he served the Government and the people of Fiji.

The Prime Minister says the Ministry will work closely with Vocea's family to coordinate funeral arrangements in accordance with established protocols.

Rabuka says his thoughts and prayers remain with Vocea's family and loved ones during this difficult time.

item.title: Education Ministry assessing drought impact on schools
item.description: The Ministry of Education is assessing the impact of the ongoing El Niño drought on schools across Fiji following the declaration of a National State of Disaster. Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the Ministry will provide further details on arrangements for the remainder of the school term as the situation develops.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Education is assessing the impact of the ongoing El Niño drought on schools across Fiji following the declaration of a National State of Disaster.

Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the Ministry will provide further details on arrangements for the remainder of the school term as the situation develops.

He says the safety of students and teachers remains a priority while ensuring that children's education continues.

Radrodro is urging parents, teachers and school communities to take necessary precautions, including storing enough water for children and limiting outdoor activities during periods of extreme heat.

He is also calling on school heads and management to closely monitor water supplies at their schools.

Radrodro says schools facing water shortages or without reliable access to water must immediately inform their District Education Officers so that assistance can be arranged.

Radrodro says schools must also have backup plans in place to ensure adequate water supplies, particularly in drought-affected areas.

He says the Ministry will continue working with the National Disaster Risk Management Office, the Water Authority of Fiji and other relevant agencies to monitor the situation and assist affected schools.

Parents, teachers and students are urged to remain vigilant and await further official announcements from the Ministry .

item.title: From Taveuni to Israel: 7 students pursue their farming dreams
item.description: Seven students from the Tutu Rural Training Centre in Taveuni have left Fiji for an 11-month agricultural internship in Israel, where they will gain hands-on experience in modern farming techniques and agricultural technology, with the aim of bringing new skills back to Fiji. The students will undergo training at the Ramat Negev International Training Centre for Advanced Agriculture, where they wi
item.content:encoded:
Seven students from the Tutu Rural Training Centre in Taveuni have left Fiji for an 11-month agricultural internship in Israel, where they will gain hands-on experience in modern farming techniques and agricultural technology, with the aim of bringing new skills back to Fiji.

The students will undergo training at the Ramat Negev International Training Centre for Advanced Agriculture, where they will learn modern farming practices and develop skills to establish and manage successful agricultural businesses.

According to the Fiji Embassy in Jerusalem, the programme aims to equip young Fijians with practical knowledge and encourage them to view agriculture as a business opportunity rather than simply a means of earning a living.

The internship is organised through MASHAV, Israel's Agency for International Development Cooperation.

T he Embassy says the opportunity follows discussions initiated by Fiji's Ambassador to Israel, Jesoni Vitusagavulu, with the Tutu Rural Training Centre in May this year.

Meanwhile, a further 24 students from the Fiji National University's College of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry and the Navuso Agricultural Training Institute are expected to join the programme in the coming weeks.

The Embassy says this will bring the total number of new Fijian students participating in the programme this year to 52.

The Fiji Embassy in Jerusalem hopes the students will use the knowledge and practical experience gained during their training to introduce improved farming practices, develop agricultural businesses and contribute to the growth of Fiji's agricultural sector when they return home.
